At 19:32:46Z it began running the action aws:ebs:volume-io-latency on gp3 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0, which is attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_6. The action adds 500 ms of latency to 100% of write I/O and 50% of read I/O, and it is set to run for 60 minutes (until about 20:32Z) with no stop condition. Each write now takes about 500 ms, so the application's outstanding I/Os pile up: VolumeQueueLength sits at about 16, which is probably the app's maximum number of in-flight I/Os. Write throughput has dropped to about 21 IOPS because the app can't complete I/O faster. Before the experiment, the volume ran a steady 500 write IOPS at about 0.95 ms average latency, well under its 3000 provisioned IOPS and 125 MiB/s. No IOPS or throughput limit-exceeded data points were recorded (VolumeIOPSExceededCheck and VolumeThroughputExceededCheck were empty). Adding IOPS would not help, because the delay is injected per operation, not caused by running out of capacity. To recover, stop the experiment with fis stop-experiment (it is set to run for 60 minutes) and add a stop condition to the template.

## Symptoms

### EBS VolumeQueueLength above threshold on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** Alarm example-d-gp3-queue-length ([redacted ARN]) has been in ALARM since 19:36:48 UTC. 3 of 3 datapoints breached the threshold of 4.0: 8.58 at 19:33, 15.998 at 19:34 and 15.998 at 19:35. The volume is gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_6 as /dev/sdf in us-east-1a.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T19:33:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: FIS 500 ms latency injection is driving the queue length up
**Description:** FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 ([redacted ARN]) is running aws:ebs:volume-io-latency against vol-0123456789abcdef0. The action adds 500 ms to all writes and half of reads. The measured latencies (~504 ms write, ~250 ms read) match these parameters. No IOPS, throughput or instance EBS limits were hit.
**Cascades to:** symptom-ebs-queue-length

#### Supporting Observations
- **FIS experiment running since 19:32:34 UTC:** FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 (template EXT1234567890abcdef_5, tag Project=example) was created at 19:32:34 UTC and is still running. That is less than 30 seconds before the first elevated queue-length datapoint. The same template ran several earlier experiments today, and users stopped them. CloudTrail shows only read calls (GetExperiment/GetExperimentTemplate) between 19:36 and 19:37.

#### Gaps
- **Application logs and metrics not checked:** Application logs and metrics on i-1234567890abcdef0_6 were not examined. The impact on the application is inferred from EBS volume metrics only.

### Root Cause: FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 injecting I/O latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0, with no stop condition
**Description:** User example-session started FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 (template EXT1234567890abcdef_5, 'example scenario d: 500 ms EBS I/O latency', role [redacted ARN]) at 19:32:35Z. At 19:32:46Z it began running aws:ebs:volume-io-latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0: +500 ms on 100% of writes and 50% of reads, for PT60M (until ~20:32:46Z). The template has stopConditions: none, so the queue-length alarm firing did not halt it. This is not a capacity problem, so adding IOPS will not help.
**Cascades to:** finding-fis-io-impairment

#### Supporting Observations
- **FIS experiment running since 19:32:34 UTC:** FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 (template EXT1234567890abcdef_5, tag Project=example) was created at 19:32:34 UTC and is still running. That is less than 30 seconds before the first elevated queue-length datapoint. The same template ran several earlier experiments today, and users stopped them. CloudTrail shows only read calls (GetExperiment/GetExperimentTemplate) between 19:36 and 19:37.
- **FIS template targets this volume with 500 ms latency and no stop condition:** Template EXT1234567890abcdef_5 (example-d-latency, 'scenario d: 500 ms EBS I/O latency') targets only vol-0123456789abcdef0. Its action is aws:ebs:volume-io-latency: +500 ms on 100% of writes and 50% of reads, for PT60M, with stopConditions: none. The template was last updated at 19:32:32 UTC. CloudTrail shows StartExperiment by example-session at 19:32:35 UTC, and the action started at 19:32:46 UTC. At a 60-minute duration it would run until about 20:32 UTC.
- **Write latency up ~500x, I/O throughput collapsed at 19:33:** From 19:03 to 19:32, vol-0123456789abcdef0 ran a steady ~30k write ops and ~30k read ops per minute (~500 IOPS each) at ~0.95 ms average write latency, with queue length 0.77. - **Read latency rose ~0.59 ms → ~250 ms; instance EBS balance unaffected:** Average read latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0 went from ~0.59 ms to ~250 ms after 19:34. The other data volume, vol-1234567890abcdef0_17, was idle (0 ops), so it gives no comparison baseline.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Stop FIS experiment EXP1234567890abcdef_7 and add the queue-length alarm as a stop condition on template EXT1234567890abcdef_5. Do not change the volume's IOPS or throughput.

## Reasoning
The experiment adds 500 ms to 100% of writes and 50% of reads on vol-0123456789abcdef0 until ~20:32:46Z (~54 more minutes of impact). Capacity limits were ruled out, so raising IOPS would only add cost. Both the template and the run have stopConditions=none, so the alarm didn't stop it. The run is tagged Project=example and the template already ran 5 times today, so it is probably a planned test: check with example-session before stopping it. The other option is to wait for it to end on its own.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Save the current template as the rollback baseline
**Type:** command
```
aws fis get-experiment-template --id EXT1234567890abcdef_5 --region us-east-1 > fis-template-EXT1234567890abcdef_5-backup.json
```
**Purpose:** Save the current template as the rollback baseline.

#### 1.2 Record the experiment's state and parameters so the test can be re-run
**Type:** command
```
aws fis get-experiment --id EXP1234567890abcdef_7 --region us-east-1 > fis-experiment-EXP1234567890abcdef_7-backup.json
```
**Purpose:** Record the experiment's state and parameters so the test can be re-run.

#### 1.3 Get the owner's agreement before ending a likely intentional test
**Type:** text
Ask example-session whether EXP1234567890abcdef_7 is an intentional test and whether it can end before its 60 minutes are up.
**Purpose:** Get the owner's agreement before ending a likely intentional test.
**Risks:** Stopping early may cut short an evaluation meant to observe the full 60 minutes.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Check the experiment is still running
**Type:** command
```
aws fis get-experiment --id EXP1234567890abcdef_7 --region us-east-1 --query 'experiment.{status:state.status,action:actions.latency.state.status}'
```
**Purpose:** Check the experiment is still running. If it already ended, skip the stop command.

#### 2.2 Record the alarm state before the change (expect ALARM)
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names example-d-gp3-queue-length --region us-east-1 --query 'MetricAlarms[0].{State:StateValue,Reason:StateReason}'
```
**Purpose:** Record the alarm state before the change (expect ALARM).

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 End the injected 500 ms I/O latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Type:** command
```
aws fis stop-experiment --id EXP1234567890abcdef_7 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** End the injected 500 ms I/O latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0.
**Risks:** The planned test ends early and its results will be incomplete.
**Advisory:** This only halts the experiment and deletes nothing. Status moves through stopping to stopped, and latency should be back to ~1 ms within a minute or two.

#### 3.2 Make future runs stop on their own when queue length stays above 4
**Type:** command
```
aws fis update-experiment-template --id EXT1234567890abcdef_5 --region us-east-1 --stop-conditions source=aws:cloudwatch:alarm,value=[redacted ARN]
```
**Purpose:** Make future runs stop on their own when queue length stays above 4.
**Risks:** Future runs will stop about 4 minutes in. If the test needs sustained degradation, use a looser guardrail alarm instead.
**Advisory:** FIS won't start an experiment while a stop-condition alarm is already in ALARM.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm the experiment reached the stopped state
**Type:** command
```
aws fis get-experiment --id EXP1234567890abcdef_7 --region us-east-1 --query 'experiment.state'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the experiment reached the stopped state.

#### 4.2 Confirm queue length is back to ~0.77, below the threshold of 4
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeQueueLength --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --start-time $(date -u -d '-15 min' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --period 60 --statistics Average --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm queue length is back to ~0.77, below the threshold of 4.

#### 4.3 Confirm the alarm returns to OK within ~3–5 minutes
**Type:** command
```

```
**Purpose:** Confirm the alarm returns to OK within ~3–5 minutes.

#### 4.4 Confirm the template now lists the alarm stop condition
**Type:** command
```
aws fis get-experiment-template --id EXT1234567890abcdef_5 --region us-east-1 --query 'experimentTemplate.stopConditions'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the template now lists the alarm stop condition.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Restore the original stop conditions if the new one gets in the way of…


**Purpose:** Restore the original stop conditions if the new one gets in the way of intended testing.
**Risks:** Future runs will again ignore the alarm.

If the owner needs the test finished, start a new run once the alarm is OK: aws fis start-experiment --experiment-template-id EXT1234567890abcdef_5 --tags Project=example --region us-east-1. A stopped experiment cannot be resumed.
**Purpose:** Re-run the evaluation if stopping it early cut it short.
**Risks:** This brings back 500 ms of I/O latency on vol-0123456789abcdef0 for 60 minutes.

### Requirements

#### 1. Give the EBS latency FIS template a guardrail stop condition in whatever creates it.
**Description:** Template EXT1234567890abcdef_5 (example-d-latency) has stopConditions source=none and was updated at 19:32:32Z. If IaC or a test harness manages it, define the stop condition there so a re-apply doesn't remove the manual change. If the test needs sustained degradation, use a looser guardrail alarm.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- get-experiment-template for EXT1234567890abcdef_5 shows at least one stopCondition with source aws:cloudwatch:alarm.
- Re-applying the IaC or harness does not reset stopConditions to source=none.
- A test run stops automatically with reason 'stop condition' when the guardrail alarm goes to ALARM.
